messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PAGER: high error rate detected for authz service due to upstream 'CacheFlare' token validation failures. Alerting oncall Maya (1812349000)

Maya (oncall): seeing 500/502 spikes from cacheflare auth API, causing our authz calls to time out and trip local rate limiter. Customer-facing 429s reported. Investigating.

Aj Patel: logs look like repeated `connect timeout` and `502 Bad Gateway` from cacheflare-auth-prod1. Rolling hist: 5xx went from ~0.2% -> 42% starting ~1812348900.

Eli: impacted flows: token validation path for hosted inference, also rate-limit check path that consults remote cache for token counts. If both fail, we fallback to local in-memory counters which are overwhelmed.

Maya (oncall): quick mitigation idea: 1) increase local cache TTL and switch rate limiter to permissive fail-open for non-SAA requests, 2) enable fallback auth bypass for internal traffic only, 3) temp reduce token verification QPS via gateway throttles. Thoughts?

Aj Patel: +1 to throttling at the gateway. Can we push a rollout to throttle suspicious backends by 30% to protect P99 latency?

Eli: I'll prepare a small rule in gateway config. Patch: `rate_limit.override = { "scope": "auth-validate", "limit": 70 }` — testing locally now.

Maya (oncall): Deploying throttle rule to prod canary group. @Support Bot please hold escalation to customers until we confirm impact.

Support Bot: noted. We'll draft status page text if this persists.

Aj Patel: Also increasing cache TTL for token cache from 60s -> 300s to reduce validation calls. Pushing config.

Maya (oncall): Command run to bump TTL:```sh
kubectl patch cm token-cache-config -n inference -p '{"data":{"TOKEN_TTL":"300"}}' && kubectl rollout restart deploy/token-cache -n inference
```

Eli: Logs after throttle + TTL bump: auth error rate dropping to ~8% after 90s. Some tenants still see 429, likely due to earlier queued requests.

Maya (oncall): Good. Need to decide long term: if CacheFlare doesn't recover, we should switch to our backup token validator (on-prem verifier). Plan: failover path to 'local-verifier' with gradual rollout. Who owns the failover runbook?

Aj Patel: I own it. Runbook step: 1) enable local-verifier feature-flag for 10% of traffic; 2) monitor evals for quality / auth mismatches; 3) ramp to 100% in 15m. I can start the canary once we confirm metrics.

Eli: Watchpoints: token revocation delay, audit logs, increased CPU on on-prem box. We'll add a CPU autoscale policy before ramp.

Maya (oncall): Adding these to incident checklist. Also contacting CacheFlare support slack channel for ETA. Message sent: "we're seeing widespread 502s on token-validate endpoint impacting multiple customers, please advise ETA and mitigation".

IncidentBot: Pager note appended: escalation level = P1, log link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/abc/authz-errors?from=1812348000&to=1812349600

Aj Patel: Support update draft for status page: "We're experiencing degraded authentication due to a third-party token validation provider. We've applied throttles and cache changes to reduce customer impact while we work with the vendor and prepare a failover. Some requests may receive 429s or increased latency. Next update in 30 minutes."

Support Bot: Draft saved to status page; scheduled to publish if error rate > 5% for next 10m.

Maya (oncall): Handoff to Aj for next 4 hours at 1812349600. I'll summarise: CacheFlare upstream returned 502s causing authz path failures and elevated 429s; mitigations applied: gateway throttle canary, token-cache TTL increased, on-prem verifier on standby. Monitoring shows error rate falling but not resolved.

Aj Patel: Taking over. I'll coordinate failover canary and escalate to infra if on-prem CPU spike. Ping me with @aj if anything urgent. :thumbsup:

Eli: I'll keep an eye on metrics and prepare autoscale policy. If CacheFlare comes back, we'll rollback throttle and TTL change after 30m stable.

Maya (oncall): Thanks team. Logging incident for postmortem and tagging vendors/support contacts. :white_check_mark:

Support Bot: Status page published at 1812350400: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-314

IncidentBot: Incident closed to oncall Maya; current owner Aj Patel.

Aj Patel: updating this thread with canary progress.
